back: Estimating the value of a variable at an unsampled place from values at nearby sample points.

notes: Estimates always lie within the range of the samples.

back: The degree to which values at nearby locations are similar (positive), dissimilar (negative) or unrelated.
Positive: clustered. About −1/(N − 1): random. Towards −1: dispersed.
About 1: random. Below 1: clustered (positive autocorrelation). Above 1: dispersed.

front: What is W in the formulae?
back: The sum of all the weights; for contiguity weights, twice the number of neighbouring pairs.
It cannot estimate values above the highest or below the lowest sample, so it misses peaks and troughs.
Between two samples the value changes in proportion to distance along the line joining them.

front: Why is the weights table important?
back: It defines who counts as a neighbour; different definitions can give different Moran's I values.
